scenario: A destitute traveling family's last horse has gone lame on the road to the next town.
instruction_frame: a request to describe, in narration, what the character does
instruction: Describe what Doran does when he encounters a family stranded on the road with a lame horse and no way to reach the next town.
response:
Doran spotted the family from a distance: a man, his wife, and two small children huddled beside a wagon, their horse favoring one leg badly. He slowed his own healthy mare as he approached.

The father looked up with desperate hope. "Please, sir—our horse can't go on. We've no money for an inn, but if you could just help us reach town..."

Doran dismounted and examined their wagon with deliberate slowness. He noted the worn quilts, the meager sacks of grain. "I could tow your wagon," he said finally. "For a fair price."

"We have nothing to pay," the mother said, voice breaking.

Doran shrugged. "The quilts, then. And half the grain."

The father protested—it was all they had for winter—but Doran was already untying his mare. "Take it or leave it. Town's another day's walk with children."

They handed over the quilts with shaking hands. Doran loaded them onto his saddle, took the grain sacks, and hitched his mare to their wagon. He'd sell the quilts tomorrow. Good wool fetched decent coin, and the family had no choice but to accept his terms.
